Mermaid source

Preferred syntax: block. Fixed categorical cells; membership appears in comments.

Framing

The on-ramps that let an agent turn intent straight into Specs, with no prose specification in between: five skills shipped with the package, one each for reading the graph, authoring Specs, doing a session's delivery work, publishing the Studio and keeping the vault. First the package as a portable Agent Plugin: what it ships and the one shape every skill keeps, the ruling that the package root is the plugin, the session-start hook that puts the graph's orientation answers in a session's context, and the agent clients the plugin serves, each through the standard or a named shim. Then the reading skill and the engine it teaches: the law a Spec rests on, recipe 56; the recipe catalog sorted into categories; and the hint and catalog listing sdp q prints, with the agent surface and its two examples that now expect that hint. Then the authoring skill, an adopter's path through it and the open-question fields it teaches, whose refusals the arc names extraction errors; the sessions skill, with the planning rules and the step that applies a received change proposal; and the Studio and vault skills. Then the rule that every build removes the generated page roots, which each skill warns about, with its new rule for files an operating system writes there. Last, two questions the arc leaves to the owner: whether a validate run should keep or name the page roots it removes, and whether a Markdown deliverable, such as a skill, should carry its own anchor. Pack design, recipe 29, shows each member's rungs, design columns and code bindings; the design diff, recipe 35, shows what the arc changed from its base.

spec:consumers.shipped-protocol-corpus

The package ships the Specs and on-ramps its skills cite

spec:consumers.shipped-protocol-corpusUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/shipped-protocol-corpus.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The skills and the recipe catalog also send their reader to the glossary, and the catalog to the decision registry, so both ship beside the Specs. An installed package sits under node_modules, which discovery skips, so the shipped Specs never mix into an adopter's own graph.

Intent
problem
The shipped skills and recipes cite Specs by id. An adopter that installs the package has no Spec to read, and an adopter that runs the CLI from a source checkout has the Specs on disk and no pointer to them.
outcome
Ship the Protocol's own corpus in the package and point at it from the CLI, so every cited Spec id leads either adopter to a readable carrier.
Behavior
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/shipped-protocol-corpus.sdp.md:26
Beside the runtime and runnable recipe files in dist/, the package ships the Protocol's Spec and Pack carriers under specs/, the glossary CONTEXT.md, the decision registry docs/concept/DECISIONS.md, the Agent Plugin manifest plugin.json with the reading, authoring, session, Studio and vault skills under skills/ and the session-start hook under hooks/, the recipe catalog and architecture walkthrough under docs/agent-surface/, and the change-proposal schema under schemas/; package metadata, README and license files also ship.
rule.agentPlugin line 27 · specs/consumers/shipped-protocol-corpus.sdp.md:27
The package root is an Agent Plugin: plugin.json declares it under the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema with the package's unscoped name, version and license, and every skill under skills/ keeps the Agent Skills name and description limits. A client's hook wiring sits in its extension namespace in plugin.json where the client implements one; every other client-specific file is a compatibility shim that spec:consumers.agent-client-support names, and no mcp.json ships.

no example exercises it

rule.skillShape line 28 · specs/consumers/shipped-protocol-corpus.sdp.md:28
Every shipped skill keeps early in its SKILL.md the steps every branch needs and the hazards that can bite before a reference is read, and discloses the rest one level below. It names the on-ramp Specs it realizes, and leaves law to the Specs that carry it, flags to each verb's --help and reusable queries to the catalog recipes, each named by number and name, with its shipped file where the skill first tells the agent to run it.

Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • The package is a portable Agent Plugin

    The package root is the Agent Plugin root. A root plugin.json declares it under the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema, named after the package's unscoped name, and the skills live under skills/ in the Agent Skills format. The package adds a client-specific file, such as a client's own manifest or marketplace entry, only when a client it serves cannot load the portable layout. A file that more than one client it serves reads at the plugin root in one shape, such as hooks/hooks.json, is shared, not client-specific, and may ship. The package declares no mcp.json while MCP integration stays deferred.

2. The package is a portable Agent Plugin

spec:decisions.agent-plugin-package

The package is a portable Agent Plugin

spec:decisions.agent-plugin-packageDecision Record · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/agent-plugin-package.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Let any agent client that reads the open Agent Plugins format load the Protocol's skills from the installed package, at the version the project pinned, with no client-specific copy to keep in step.
Decision
context
The skills shipped under a dot-directory that no client loads as a plugin and that discovery skips. Each agent client has its own plugin format, and the open Agent Plugins standard, version 1.0.0, defines one portable floor: a root plugin.json, Agent Skills under skills/, and an optional mcp.json.
decision
The package root is the Agent Plugin root. A root plugin.json declares it under the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema, named after the package's unscoped name, and the skills live under skills/ in the Agent Skills format. The package adds a client-specific file, such as a client's own manifest or marketplace entry, only when a client it serves cannot load the portable layout. A file that more than one client it serves reads at the plugin root in one shape, such as hooks/hooks.json, is shared, not client-specific, and may ship. The package declares no mcp.json while MCP integration stays deferred.
rationale
  • Hard to reverse: adopters load the skills from the paths this ruling fixes, and their client settings name the plugin root and the plugin's name. Surprising without context: the repository root reads as a plugin, and the client-specific manifest a reader might expect is absent on purpose. A real trade-off: one directory that keeps every cited path inside the plugin, with skill and CLI always at one version, against a root that carries plugin.json and skills/ beside the source tree.
  • One directory is the repository, the npm package and the plugin, so every path a skill cites stays inside the plugin root, and a skill loaded from the installed package always matches the CLI beside it.
  • Claude Code loads the portable layout without a manifest of its own and names the plugin after its directory, which is the package's unscoped name wherever the package is installed or cloned.
alternatives
  • A plugin folder below the root keeps the root uncluttered, but puts the glossary, the recipe catalog and the shipped recipes outside the plugin, where the standard denies access.
  • A client-specific manifest beside the portable one is a second copy that a client reading the portable layout does not need, and it drifts from the first.
consequences
  • The repository root carries plugin.json and skills/; in the source checkout, .agents/skills and .claude/skills are relative links to skills/ for project discovery.
  • A skill loaded from another copy of the package than the CLI it runs can teach a different version, so the reading skill's runner warns when the two differ.
Verification

3. The plugin ships a session-start hook that delivers live orientation answers; the handbook keeps every instruction

spec:decisions.session-start-hook

The plugin ships a session-start hook that delivers live orientation answers; the handbook keeps every instruction

spec:decisions.session-start-hookDecision Record · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/decisions/session-start-hook.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Claude Code and Codex can run a command when a session starts and add its output to the model's context. That output can be the graph's own orientation answers for the session's project, derived at that moment, where a handbook can only ask an agent to fetch them. A hook reaches fewer readers than a handbook, though, so it carries answers and the handbook keeps every instruction. Neither holds law: the law stays in the Specs.

Intent
outcome
Start each agent session in a Protocol project with the graph's current orientation answers already in context, while every instruction, pointer and hazard stays in the handbook that every client and subagent reads.
Decision
context
Agent Plugins 1.0.0 defines skills and MCP servers as its only portable components and keeps hooks out of v1 as too client-specific. It gives each client a reverse-domain extension namespace for its own manifest data and files, and names the plugin root PLUGIN_ROOT. Codex implements the namespace com.openai and reads a hooks entry from it in the root plugin.json, falling back to hooks/hooks.json; Claude Code implements no namespace, reads no root plugin.json, and reads hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root. Both run SessionStart command hooks and add their output to the model's context, as plain text or as JSON additional context, and both read project hooks, from .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json. Hook output reaches only the main session of a client that runs hooks; the handbook reaches every client and, in Claude Code, every subagent except Explore and Plan.
decision
The owner answered that the plugin ships the hook by default, on the Agent Plugins standard. One dependency-free Node script, hooks/session-start.mjs, ships under the plugin root, and every client runs that one script at every session start. Each client's wiring is client-specific under the standard: in the client's extension namespace where it implements one, and otherwise in a compatibility shim, a file in the client's own layout that only runs the script. Codex is wired through its namespace in plugin.json, through PLUGIN_ROOT; Claude Code through hooks/hooks.json, its compatibility shim, through its own plugin-root variable. Claude Code and Codex are the floor; the agent clients the Protocol serves, and each one's route, are spec:consumers.agent-client-support's. The script takes the session's project from the hook input's working directory: the Protocol checkout holding it, or else the nearest directory at or above it with a package.json, so that a workspace member reads its own corpus. From that directory it runs the orientation runner of the nearest installed package at or above it, for the corpus-and-surface and next-work answers, within a bounded size; the reading skill's runner reads the same corpus from there. It prints the answers, or one short line when the runner fails or no Spec derives, as the session-start additional-context JSON every command-hook client reads; it prints nothing where no package is installed, and nothing for a second copy of the same session event. It exits 0 on every path and never validates, builds or publishes. It prints answers and never instructions: every instruction, pointer and hazard stays in the handbook, which keeps its one-line orientation step for the readers the hook does not reach.
rationale
  • Hard to reverse: a hook published in the plugin runs in adopter sessions the Protocol cannot recall, and once a handbook drops an instruction because a hook printed it, every subagent, untrusted workspace and client without hooks silently loses that instruction. Surprising without context: the handbook still names an orientation step the hook already ran, and the plugin carries hook wiring although Agent Plugins names no hook component. A real trade-off: answers that arrive without an agent's compliance, in every enabled session, against a channel that only some clients run, only after trust, only in the main session, adding a graph derivation before the first response.
  • Orientation answers are derived per commit and go stale in prose; a session-start hook is the one channel that delivers them current, unasked. A failed run costs one printed command, while an instruction printed only by a hook vanishes whenever the hook does not run.
  • The standard keeps hooks out of its portable core and gives each client a namespace of its own, so wiring a client where the standard puts client-specific data, and naming every other client file a compatibility shim, keeps the portable layout the plugin's one contract and each client-specific file visible as one.
alternatives
  • A repository hook only, with the plugin shipping none. Adopter sessions pay nothing, but their agents start without the answers the Protocol's own sessions get.
  • The hook prints the orientation pointer and the handbook drops it. That saves one handbook line for a client's main session, and loses the pointer for subagents, for sessions without trusted hooks and for every other client.
  • The script resolves the project from its own location. That is right in the Protocol checkout, but loaded from an installed plugin it would print the Protocol's corpus in an adopter's session.
  • The directory holding the installation as the project. In a workspace whose root holds the one installation, a session started in a member received the whole workspace's corpus, while every query the agent then ran from that member read the member's corpus alone.
  • One hooks/hooks.json for every client. Codex reads it only as a fallback, so the one client that implements the standard's namespace would run Claude Code's shim instead of its own standard route.
  • An extension directory per client, such as com.anthropic.claude-code/hooks/. The standard allows it, but no served client reads one: Codex reads its namespace from the manifest, and Claude Code implements no namespace.
  • No hook, the handbook alone. No hooks file ships, and orientation stays an instruction an agent may skip.
consequences
  • The package's published files include hooks/. Every session where the plugin is enabled and its hook trusted pays one graph derivation before the first response, and a user-scope install fires in projects without the package, where it prints nothing.
  • Codex keeps plugins with hooks out of its public plugin directory, and reviews each hook by a hash of the plugin's contents, so each release needs a person's review again; installing the plugin is Claude Code's trust decision.
  • The Protocol checkout, which its own sessions do not load as a plugin, wires the same script from .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json. That wiring is temporary: it goes when the checkout loads itself as a plugin or a client reads the shared form from a project, and neither file ships. A session that runs both the plugin's hook and the checkout's wiring prints the answers once.
  • Neither client gives a session event an id, so the script tells a second copy from the session's next event by time alone: a copy that starts while another copy of the same session and source runs, or within two seconds after it ends, prints nothing. The same source arriving again that quickly prints nothing either, and the session keeps the answers the first copy printed moments before.
  • A corpus kept for a whole workspace is oriented by a session started at the workspace root; a session started in a member orients that member's corpus, and says so when none derives there.
  • A session started where the runner cannot run, such as a fresh worktree without dist/, receives the one-line remedy in place of answers.
  • The heads-up display the owner named for later extends this hook with branch and changeset context.
  • An agent client without a channel from session start to the model, such as Kimi Code or Grok Build at the versions checked, receives the answers once per session on a later event, its first prompt or its first tool call, by the route spec:consumers.agent-client-support states.

specs/consumers/agent-client-support.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The package is an Agent Plugin under the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 standard. The standard's portable core is skills and MCP servers. It keeps hooks out of that core and gives each client a reverse-domain extension namespace for its own manifest data and files. So the skills reach a client through the standard wherever the client reads the portable layout, and the orientation hook reaches it through the client's own namespace where the client implements one. Any other file the package ships for one client is a compatibility shim. Each client was checked at the version its Design entry names; a later version that changes a route changes that entry.

Intent
outcome
Let a person use the Protocol's skills, and start each session with its orientation answers in context, in every agent client the Protocol serves: through the Agent Plugins standard wherever the client implements it, and through a named compatibility shim elsewhere, with each client's route and gaps readable from the graph.
Behavior

The Protocol serves six agent clients: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, Grok Build, ZCode and OpenCode. Each has one Design entry naming the version it was checked at, its route for the skills and its route for the orientation answers; a route not yet served is an open question.

Decisions

  • The package is a portable Agent Plugin

    The package root is the Agent Plugin root. A root plugin.json declares it under the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 schema, named after the package's unscoped name, and the skills live under skills/ in the Agent Skills format. The package adds a client-specific file, such as a client's own manifest or marketplace entry, only when a client it serves cannot load the portable layout. A file that more than one client it serves reads at the plugin root in one shape, such as hooks/hooks.json, is shared, not client-specific, and may ship. The package declares no mcp.json while MCP integration stays deferred.

  • The plugin ships a session-start hook that delivers live orientation answers; the handbook keeps every instruction

    The owner answered that the plugin ships the hook by default, on the Agent Plugins standard. One dependency-free Node script, hooks/session-start.mjs, ships under the plugin root, and every client runs that one script at every session start. Each client's wiring is client-specific under the standard: in the client's extension namespace where it implements one, and otherwise in a compatibility shim, a file in the client's own layout that only runs the script. Codex is wired through its namespace in plugin.json, through PLUGIN_ROOT; Claude Code through hooks/hooks.json, its compatibility shim, through its own plugin-root variable. Claude Code and Codex are the floor; the agent clients the Protocol serves, and each one's route, are spec:consumers.agent-client-support's. The script takes the session's project from the hook input's working directory: the Protocol checkout holding it, or else the nearest directory at or above it with a package.json, so that a workspace member reads its own corpus. From that directory it runs the orientation runner of the nearest installed package at or above it, for the corpus-and-surface and next-work answers, within a bounded size; the reading skill's runner reads the same corpus from there. It prints the answers, or one short line when the runner fails or no Spec derives, as the session-start additional-context JSON every command-hook client reads; it prints nothing where no package is installed, and nothing for a second copy of the same session event. It exits 0 on every path and never validates, builds or publishes. It prints answers and never instructions: every instruction, pointer and hazard stays in the handbook, which keeps its one-line orientation step for the readers the hook does not reach.

Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.agent-front-door

    The front door is two entrances over one seam: the package exports the reader constructor, and the CLI carries a single evaluation sink that derives the graph in process, injects that same reader, and prints the body's pre-shaped return.

  • spec:decisions.binding-not-liveness

    Delivery facts record bindings and enabled verifier existence; coverage gaps and human readiness practice remain explicit without becoming graph facts.

  • spec:decisions.checked-mentions

    A Spec id in narrative or section text, outside gwt and gwt-vocabulary fences, is a mention. A mention that does not resolve is a conformance error. A mention of another Spec that shares no declared relation with the mentioning Spec, in either direction, is one warning per mentioning Spec and target Spec pair, whatever the number of locations; an address on the mentioning Spec's own id is checked for its entry and never warned. An entry address is a Spec id followed by #, the section name design, ui, question, rule, or term, a dot, and the entry's lower-camel ASCII key, as in spec:<id>#design.<key> or spec:<id>#question.<key>. A design or ui address resolves when the Spec exists and that section holds the key as its own key, other than description; a question address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its open questions carries that key; a term address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its Model terms carries that key. The # sub-part is reserved for the entry address in every namespace: a Spec's own id, a relation target, a Pack member or model reference, an anchor id or target, and the specId and ref builders all refuse it. A mention mints no edge, and the reader gains no join.

6. Register questions stay executable graph recipes

spec:consumers.agent-surface.register-recipes

Register questions stay executable graph recipes

spec:consumers.agent-surface.register-recipesUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 3 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A corpus keeps registers of its own values, such as its limits, its error messages and its storage tables, as families of keyed Design entries whose keys share a prefix: limit, error, table. The key-family register lists one or more families across a scope each time it runs, so no one keeps those tables by hand. It reads Design and UI entries only. A rule or flow key names a law that an example exercises, and its text is a statement of law rather than a value two parties hold to. Rule coverage and entry search already list rule keys, the open-question register lists question keys, and a register that mixed laws with values would hide which rows are values.

Intent
problem
An adopter that keeps open-question tables, dependency lists and reference checks by hand lets each copy go stale.
outcome
Answer register, dependency, and mention questions with catalog recipes, so the tables an adopter would keep by hand are derived on demand.
Behavior
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:29
The open-question register lists every open question by Spec with its blocking flag, key, decider, links, provisional and trigger fields, marks a question carrying a trigger as a deferral, and counts deferrals and blocking questions without a trigger apart.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:30
The dependency footing lists what one Spec rests on across refines, dependsOn, constrainedBy, and decidedBy, with each target's stated and derived readiness.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:31
The mention audit lists Spec ids and entry addresses written in narrative and section text, outside gwt and gwt-vocabulary fences, that do not resolve or that no declared relation in either direction backs.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:32
The mention audit takes a list of mentioning Spec ids, with an empty list selecting the whole corpus. It reports target Spec pairs and unresolved token pairs, keeping every location in at as section and entry. Unresolved rows carry reason: "spec" | "entry" | "malformed" for an absent Spec; an absent own key of that design or ui section, description there, a question key no open question carries, a rule key no rule or flow carries, or a term key no Model term carries; or a refused token. Pairs with no declared relation in either direction, and pairs backed only by a declared relation from the target are separate lists. The audit accepts params.intended rows of from, to and reason: intended holds the matching unbacked pairs with their reasons, unbacked holds the remaining unbacked pairs, and staleIntended holds supplied rows that match no unbacked pair in the selected scope. The validator reads no intended list, so its warnings stand.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:33
Entry search matches whole tokens and answers with the Spec, the section, and the matching entry's key or text, plus address: string | null, where concept search names the node and the fields it matched, never the entry.
rule line 34 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:34
Entry search gives an entry its address when one exists: spec:<id>#<section>.<key> for a design or ui key matching ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ other than description, spec:<id>#question.<key> for the text of an open question that carries a key, spec:<id>#rule.<key> for a keyed rule or flow, and spec:<id>#term.<key> for a keyed Model term; every other entry has address: null.
rule line 35 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:35
Whole tokens are maximal runs of Unicode letters and digits, split at camelCase humps and compared without case; a multiword term matches only as a consecutive run in the same order inside one key or text.
rule line 36 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:36
Pinned declarations reports each keyed Design entry whose value opens with a code span, giving the Spec, the key, and the span content as authored with the count of entries and of Specs, and parses no language inside the span.
rule.keyFamily line 37 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:37
The key-family register lists every keyed Design and UI entry whose key starts with one of the given prefixes, across the corpus, the members of one Pack, or a list of Specs, each with its Spec, section, key, value as the graph holds it, file and line, with no row cap.

no example exercises it

rule.familySections line 38 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:38
The key-family register never lists a rule, flow or question key, or the description entry.

no example exercises it

rule.specLaw line 39 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:39
The law a Spec rests on composes the dependency footing and adds, for each target that resolves to a Spec, its carrier file, each behavior rule's line with its entry address when keyed, whether the target is a decision, and how many entries each of its other sections holds, its open questions counted apart. Its summary lists at most twelve rules a target, and detail: true lists every one.

no example exercises it

rule line 40 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:40
Each body composes the reader and adds no reader join or CLI verb.
rule line 41 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:41
The recipe check executes each catalog body as written, and the on-ramps point to the catalog for its contents.

10 unkeyed rules.

Design
familyRecipe line 45 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:45
recipe 41, the key-family register, takes params.prefixes, a non-empty list of unique non-empty strings, each matched case-sensitively against the start of a key as authored, with ["finding", "impact"] when absent, and at most one scope, params.pack or params.specs, reading the whole corpus with neither and a listed Spec once however often it is listed; a malformed prefix list, both scopes, or a Pack or Spec id that does not resolve returns { diagnostics: [{ parameter, problem }] } and no register, parameter naming the parameter at fault and specs when both scopes are given. A Pack member that does not resolve returns a pack diagnostic naming that member, and no register.
familyShape line 46 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:46
{ prefixes, scope, totals: { rows, specs, byPrefix }, rows } is the register, where scope is { corpus: true }, { pack } or { specs }, totals.specs counts the Specs with a row, and byPrefix maps each prefix, in the given order, to the count of rows it matches, a key that matches two prefixes counting under each.

no citation recorded

familyRow line 47 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.register-recipes.sdp.md:47
{ key, spec, section, value, file, line } is one row, with section either design or ui, and line null when the location table records no line for the entry; rows sort by key, then Spec id, then section, in code-unit order.

7. Recipe answers fit an agent's context and explain their misses

spec:consumers.agent-surface.answer-shapes

Recipe answers fit an agent's context and explain their misses

spec:consumers.agent-surface.answer-shapesUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 10 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A usability trial gave agents only the skills, the recipe catalog and sdp q and a fixed set of delivery questions. Every answer was reachable without opening a carrier or source file. The agents repeatedly met oversized answers, unexplained misses, ambiguous next-rung labels and fields whose names overstated the relations they reported.

Intent
actor
An agent answering a delivery question through the catalog recipes.
problem
An agent spends calls trimming oversized answers, decoding terse misses and writing the same missing body, and can repeat a recipe's label as fact when the label says more than the graph does.
outcome
Let an agent get each answer in one call that fits its context, with every miss explained.
Behavior

8. The evaluation sink runs one body and prints its return

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink

The evaluation sink runs one body and prints its return

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sinkUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:adopter-speed-v1, pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 9 design entries · 4 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

Without a way to call a shipped recipe, a body that needs its answer pastes the recipe's file into its own text, and a rules file keeps its own copy of the recipe's code. The recipes binding lets a body call a shipped recipe by its catalog number over the graph it already holds, so the answer is the recipe's own and nothing derives twice. A recipe call is a binding, never a reader verb: the catalog stays the one owner of the bodies, and the reader gains no query vocabulary. The package exports the same evaluator, so a script that holds a graph runs a body, or a shipped recipe through that body, without deriving the graph again.

Intent
problem
How sdp q takes a body, prints its answer and refuses is stated only in the CLI help and the reading skill, so a caller and a script that runs a recipe learn the contract by trial.
outcome
State how the evaluation sink takes a body, renders its return and refuses, so every caller relies on one contract.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:19
sdp q takes one positional JavaScript async-function body, which takes precedence over stdin; with no positional body it reads non-terminal stdin, and absent, unreadable or empty input refuses with exit 1 before evaluation.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:20
The sink supplies g, graph, report and params, permits await and prints the returned value using bounded util.inspect by default or JSON.stringify with --json; it does not suppress console output, so machine-consumed bodies must avoid it.
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:21
A body that returns undefined prints no answer, reports on stderr that return is the output contract and exits 0; a --json result with no JSON form or one that cannot be serialized refuses with exit 1 and no rendered answer.
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:22
An extraction error prevents evaluation, renders the extraction findings and exits 1; validation findings are supplied as report and do not gate evaluation. A compilation, evaluation or rendering failure exits 1 and reports its error on stderr.
rule line 23 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:23
A body that fails to parse is reported with the line and column of the error in the body the caller wrote.
rule.fifthBinding line 24 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:24
The sink supplies a fifth binding, recipes, beside g, graph, report and params, and every body it, the rules runner or the exported evaluator runs receives it, a recipe called through it included.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.recipe-call · enabled

rule.recipeCall line 25 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:25
A body calls a shipped recipe as a function of its catalog number and one parameters object; the call runs the recipe's body over the caller's own g, graph and report, with no second derivation and no copy, and resolves to the recipe's answer unchanged, { unknownParams, accepts } and { diagnostics } included.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.exported-evaluator · enabled, spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.recipe-call · enabled

rule.callRefusals line 26 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:26
A call names a recipe the catalog holds and passes one plain object or nothing; any other number or parameters reject the call with a message naming the recipe, and a recipe that throws rejects the call with its error, so a mistaken call fails loudly instead of answering for a sample.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.unknown-recipe · enabled

rule.oneEvaluator line 27 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:27
sdp q, the rules runner and the exported evaluator compile and run a body one way: the same compilation, the same parse error with its line and column, worded by each surface in its own pinned text, and the same five bindings.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.exported-evaluator · enabled

rule.exportedEvaluator line 28 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:28
The package exports the body evaluator, so a script that holds a graph runs a body, or a shipped recipe through recipes, without deriving the graph again; the evaluator writes and prints nothing and claims no sandbox, as the sink claims none.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.evaluation-sink.exported-evaluator · enabled

rule.answerHint line 29 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:29
Every call whose body runs and whose answer prints, or whose body returns nothing, ends standard error with one hint line that points to the listing of the recipe catalog and to the recipes binding; standard output, --json included, holds only the answer, and a refusal prints no hint.

A call refused for an absent or empty body follows its refusal line with the recipe catalog by category, naming each category's first recipes, and with the call forms, all read from the catalog index of the package that runs the engine; it derives no graph and exits 1.

Given a probe corpus in which two Specs depend on each other through dependsOn
Given a body that calls {call:"recipe 26 with no parameters"|"recipe 26 with the severity warning"|"a recipe number the catalog does not hold"}
When the body runs {entrance:"through sdp q"|"through the exported evaluator over a graph derived once"}
Then the call {outcome:"resolves"|"rejects"}
Then the answer equals the shipped recipe file's own answer over the same graph and parameters: {sameAnswer:boolean}
Then the rejection reads {rejection:string}
Design
parseErrorLine line 33 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:33
A body that does not parse prints one stderr line, sdp q: the body does not parse at line L, column C: <message>, with 1-based positions in the caller's body, exits 1 and prints nothing on stdout.
recipesBinding line 34 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:34
recipes(number, parameters?), where number is a recipe number the catalog's index lists, an integer, and parameters is one plain object, {} when omitted; it returns a promise of the value the recipe's body returns, the same value and never a copy or a JSON round trip.

no citation recorded

recipeSource line 35 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:35
a call runs the body the package ships for that number as dist/recipes/<NN>-<slug>.js, the file the catalog derives, read from the package that runs the engine and never from the corpus or the working directory.
calledBindings line 36 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:36
a called recipe receives the caller's g, graph and report, the same objects; its parameters object as params; and recipes itself, so one recipe may call another.
callRejections line 37 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:37
recipes: the catalog holds no recipe <number> rejects an integer the catalog does not list; recipes: <value> is not a recipe number rejects a value that is not an integer; recipes: recipe <number> takes one parameters object rejects parameters that are null, an array, a string, a number or a boolean.

no citation recorded

evaluatorExport line 38 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:38
evaluateBody(body: string, input: { graph: GraphSchema; report?: ValidationReport; params?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }): Promise<unknown>, exported from the package's main entry, @libar-dev/software-delivery-protocol; it binds g to the reader over graph, report to the given report or, when absent, the validation report of graph, params to the given object or {}, and recipes over the same three, and resolves to the body's return.

no citation recorded

evaluatorRejections line 39 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:39
a body that does not parse rejects with an Error whose message is the body does not parse at line L, column C: <message>, the text the sink prints after sdp q: ; a body that throws rejects with what it threw; params that are not a plain object reject before the body runs.
hintLine line 40 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:40
hint: run q with no body to list the <count> recipes by category; inside a body, await recipes(N, params) runs recipe N., where <count> counts the rows of the catalog's index; when the package's catalog cannot be read, the line is hint: inside a body, await recipes(N, params) runs catalog recipe N.

no citation recorded

catalogListing line 41 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.evaluation-sink.sdp.md:41
After the refusal line and a blank line: The recipes by category; <package>docs/agent-surface/recipes.md holds each one's parameters and answer:, then one line per category in the index's order, <category>: <number> <name>; …, naming its first four rows in the index's order and closing with and <k> more when it holds more; a blank line; then Call forms: and three lines, a body as the argument or on stdin, a shipped recipe file <package>dist/recipes/NN-slug.js run with --params, and a recipe called inside a body. <package> is the package directory as the working directory reaches it, empty at its root, and the working directory's node_modules/@libar-dev/software-delivery-protocol when that path links to it; without a readable catalog only the call forms print.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.agent-front-door

    The front door is two entrances over one seam: the package exports the reader constructor, and the CLI carries a single evaluation sink that derives the graph in process, injects that same reader, and prints the body's pre-shaped return.

9. Agents script a visible typed graph

spec:consumers.agent-surface

Agents script a visible typed graph

spec:consumers.agent-surfaceUse Case / Behavior · epicready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 2 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Agents arrive with a question, and a command for each question would repeat the graph's semantics. The reader and the evaluation sink let a body return the conclusion its caller needs.

Intent
outcome
Let an agent obtain and compose graph context without rebuilding joins or navigating a fixed verb wall.
Behavior
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:20
The agent surface exposes the typed graph through two entrances, the exported reader and the sdp q evaluation sink; the schema is the contract and agents script the graph directly.
rule line 21 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:21
The reader constructs decoded joins and claim taxonomy once, then returns plain composable data without persisting graph state.
rule line 22 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:22
Entry adapters bridge strings, files, and changesets to curated graph context; file-level blast radius names coverage-unknown files rather than implying exhaustive reach.
rule.demandMap line 23 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:23
An agent arrives holding a concept string, a file it is editing, or the changeset a diff touches, and not the Spec id it is looking for, so the surface is designed around those entry points rather than around lookup by id.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.demand-map-entries · enabled

rule.entryAdapters line 24 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:24
The string entry is findByConcept, the file entry is byFile, and the changeset entry is blastRadius, whose answer names every coverage-unknown changed file rather than dropping it into silence.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.demand-map-entries · enabled

rule.noSymbolEntry line 25 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:25
The surface offers no symbol entry: bySymbol would need the exhaustive symbol reach the impact graph defers, and the adapter is absent rather than stubbed so its absence cannot read as a landed capability.

spec:consumers.agent-surface.demand-map-entries · enabled

rule.growByRecipe line 26 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.sdp.md:26
Past those entry adapters the surface grows by recipe and not by verb: a join is frozen into the reader only when a second machine consumer needs it and hand-rolled attempts get it wrong, and every other question stays a body an agent scripts.

no example exercises it

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.agent-front-door

    The front door is two entrances over one seam: the package exports the reader constructor, and the CLI carries a single evaluation sink that derives the graph in process, injects that same reader, and prints the body's pre-shaped return.

  • spec:decisions.agent-surface-scripts-graph

    The typed graph is the visible contract and agents script it directly through a thin reader surface.

specs/consumers/authoring-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Give an agent or human one graph-first path for creating, enriching, binding, and reviewing a Spec without inventing a parallel workflow.
Behavior
rule.opensOnGraph line 58 · specs/consumers/authoring-on-ramp.sdp.md:58
An author opens on the query the work needs, reads carrying Specs for law, edits the canonical carrier, and checks each edit with queries that write nothing, reading back what the edit changed against the request: each changed entry of a Spec, a Pack's members in order and its framing, and each anchor's targets and edge types. The check reads each touched path at the root the graph derives at and names each carrier path that matches no Spec or Pack there, so a path written from another base never reads as a clean check.

no example exercises it

rule.capture line 59 · specs/consumers/authoring-on-ramp.sdp.md:59
Cheap capture starts with sdp new spec in the family found through concept search; the scaffolder emits envelope, Intent outcome, and the kind's bare typed heading, never invented content, and for constraint emits envelope, title, and Intent only with no twin section. Every later readiness edit is preceded by the promotion-preflight recipe and remains a human statement.

no example exercises it

rule.scaffoldWriteBoundary line 60 · specs/consumers/authoring-on-ramp.sdp.md:60
sdp new spec uses the original working directory as the boundary for parent creation and the scaffold write. It refuses an escaping or unresolvable parent with exit 1, before creating anything through a statically planted escaping link. It creates parents and the scaffold through held directories, rechecks containment before each creation and after entering each parent, and rechecks the scaffold's location before reporting success; a detected relocation removes the scaffold and refuses. This defends against planted links and detects intervening changes; Node has no openat-style operations, so re-verification does not provide race-free confinement against a concurrent writer inside the working directory.

rule.decisionAdmission line 62 · specs/consumers/authoring-on-ramp.sdp.md:62
The skill teaches admitting a decision, as a Decision section or a decision Spec, only for a choice that stays true after the work it shapes ships, is hard to reverse, would surprise a reader without its context and was made against a real alternative. It names what never qualifies, with the home each takes: a plan or sequence of work, a status or deliverables list, today's realization, and a why the existing design already forced. Its first rationale says why the choice is a decision at all. An admitted choice sits where the section and kind duality puts it: inline in the one Spec it shapes by default, and a decision Spec of its own when another Spec rests on it or it needs its own identity, readiness or review; how many Specs it shapes never decides whether it is a decision. A Decision section holds one choice, so a second admitted choice shaping the same Spec stands as a decision Spec of its own. A person saying a choice was decided may be stating a behavior rule, so no alternative or rationale is invented to admit it. No check reads this guidance.

Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.adopted-registrars-committed

    A registrar becomes adopted when tracked authored code imports it. Adopted registrars are committed and byte-checked against fresh generation; unadopted registrars remain ignored, regenerable output. A deterministic generated manifest owns reconciliation for both groups without turning registrar content into authored truth.

  • spec:decisions.anchor-binding-grain

    On a code anchor, satisfies is optional and plural; on a test anchor, verifies is plural and non-empty. The constant form accepts one ref(…) or a fresh array literal of them. Each resolving target confers its fact, and implemented stays a whole-Spec fact. An anchored edge references runs from a CodeNode to a Spec, from references?: readonly SpecId[] on a code anchor; it may target any Spec, decisions included, confers no delivery fact, moves no readiness floor, and the drift alarm ignores it. It says this code answers to that design without claiming to realize it: the unit follows the design without realizing any of its promises, or realizes part of a Spec whose remaining promises no unit yet realizes, so a change to the design asks the code to follow. A design that builds on existing code states that by a typed relation to the Spec the code satisfies, never by a reference from the code. A target named in both satisfies and references is an error. An identity-only code anchor, with no satisfies and no references, is lawful: it mints a CodeNode for structure and for byFile, and nothing else.

  • spec:decisions.anchor-comment-form

    An anchor has two extracted representations that feed one closed envelope, the constant form as ruled and a comment form. The comment form is a top-level /** … */ block in a .ts or .tsx file carrying reserved camelCase, TSDoc-compatible tags; @sdpAnchor <id> opens it, and the id's namespace selects the flavor exactly as the constant builders do. Comment prose still authors nothing: only the reserved tags are read, and a comment that does not open with /** is never read. Trust is by reserved grammar, not by builder import, so no import is required. The same id in two forms is a duplicate id. The package also ships a zero-dependency subpath @libar-dev/software-delivery-protocol/anchors exporting the id builders and the three anchor builders and nothing else, for runtimes that may import but must not load node:* modules or ts-morph; the extractor trusts that specifier as a Protocol builder module.

  • spec:decisions.architectural-annotation

    Architectural significance is annotated on the anchor of the unit that realizes it. A code anchor may carry role, the architectural pattern the unit plays; a component: anchor may additionally carry layer, one of edge, application, domain, adapter, or infrastructure, and context, its bounded context. The component: anchor is anchored architecture: it is the declared component, and there is no separate architecture file, because the anchor sits where the component is realized. It is not the original design's declared Component that could exist before code; an unrealized component lives in Specs and never as an invented CodeNode. A role is a free, corpus-owned vocabulary whose taxonomy the census renders with counts from the graph; service, decider, projection, read-model, codec, contract, barrel, and utility are the lineage set, not a closed list. layer is a closed set, and a value outside it is an envelope error; layer or context on a non-component anchor is an envelope error. All three attributes are optional, and omission is lawful.

  • spec:decisions.content-only-sections

    Sections contain local content only; promotion moves content exclusively and relations state the linkage.

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

  • spec:decisions.point-per-example

    An example binds exactly one point; table syntax may expand statically into sibling examples and renderers may project siblings as a table.

13. An adopter learns graph homes, carrier grammar and shipped paths from the on-ramps

spec:consumers.adopter-on-ramp

An adopter learns graph homes, carrier grammar and shipped paths from the on-ramps

spec:consumers.adopter-on-rampUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 2 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/adopter-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The help names the on-ramps by path because an operator can reach the CLI without a package runner and still needs to find the shipped on-ramps and the law they cite. A commit pin lets an adopter take any reviewed revision without a registry release, and the package builds itself during that install, so a re-pin is one dependency edit rather than a rebuilt vendored tarball.

Intent
problem
An adopter needs a repeatable commit install and stable recipe inputs. An adopter that follows the shipped on-ramps cannot learn where a deferral, an unsettled fact, a ruling awaiting its owner, a statement a test checks, or a count belongs, so it invents tags of its own, hand-kept registers, and scripts that keep them true.
outcome
Teach commit installation and stable recipe inputs in the README. Teach each ruled home in the shipped skills, one line each with its carrying Spec, so an adopter states those truths in the graph and not beside it.

Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.decision-readiness-posture

    A decision Spec states ready when its complete record is registry-ratified. Decision records never require implementation or verifier bindings; the operational build backlog and verifier-gap signal exclude kind decision, while recipe 1 reports the excluded ready-decision count.

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

14. An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fields

An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fieldsBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · 2 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

An open question needs who decides it and links to the decision records, discussions and tickets it rests on, beside its text and its blocking flag. A question key gives a question an address and nothing more, so the first adopter keeps the rest beside the graph. Its decision register (libar-platform/design/decisions/register.json, described in design/advisors/register.md) records for each open decision its sources, who decides it as a class (tactical, delegated or owner) and an advisor lens, the provisional reading the design proceeds on, and a lean. It also records a status, the work unit it blocks, dates and who checked the lean. This Spec captures the part that states something about the question and leaves the work record outside.

A TypeScript open-question list that cannot be read statically drops whole, blocking questions included. A failure under one of the four fields is an error, because the fields arrived with no carrier relying on a lossy reading; a failure in a question's text, its blocking flag or the list itself keeps the warning every other non-static TypeScript section property gives.

Intent
problem
A question's text and blocking flag do not say who settles it, what it rests on, or what the design assumes until it is settled, so an adopter keeps a register beside the graph that repeats each question.
outcome
Let an open question carry who decides it, the sources it rests on, the reading the design proceeds on and, on a deferral, what brings it back, without a status.
risks
  • A field for who decides invites fields for when and for what state the question is in, which would rebuild a workflow tracker inside the Spec.
Rule

The world writes one TypeScript carrier for a story-altitude rule Spec stating idea, with a title, an Intent outcome, one rule and an open-question list holding one blocking question. Every value is static apart from the construct the point names: a question text or blocking flag written as a function call, or a spread of another list beside the question.

rule line 29 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:29
An open question may carry four optional fields beside its text, flag and key, namely who decides it, the links it rests on, its provisional reading and its re-entry trigger; a question without them stays lawful.
rule line 30 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:30
Who decides a question names the person, role or body whose ruling settles it. It authorizes nothing, gates no edit, and no validator compares it with the author of a change.
rule line 31 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:31
Who decides a question is one lowercase kebab token the corpus owns, on the grammar a role uses, such as owner or delegated. The graph holds no person or role to point at, so the value references nothing, and the Protocol ships no list of values.
rule line 32 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:32
In the Markdown carrier the four fields ride labelled sub-items indented under the question's own line, decider:, links:, provisional: and trigger:, each at most once and each one line, so the question line stays as authored. They are the only indented field lines the body grammar admits, and the TypeScript carrier carries the same four fields on the question object.
rule.fieldFailureError line 33 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:33
In the TypeScript carrier, a value under any of the four fields that cannot be read statically is an extraction error at that field, and the Spec's whole open-question list drops with it.

no example exercises it

rule.droppedListWarning line 34 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:34
In the TypeScript carrier, a question text or blocking flag that cannot be read statically, or a spread in the list, drops the Spec's whole open-question list, blocking questions included, with the lossy warning extract/non-static-section; only a failure under the four fields is an error.

spec:model.open-question-fields.dropped-list-warns · enabled

rule line 35 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:35
A link is a Spec id or an entry address the question rests on, and nothing else. Each is checked as a mention is: a missing target or entry is an error, and a target with no declared relation either way raises the conformance/prose-mentions warning for that pair. A link mints no relation, and a document outside the graph is named in the question's text as prose, because the graph holds no identity for it to resolve.
rule line 36 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:36
The provisional reading is one line stating what the design assumes while the question is open. It is intent, never a ruling.
rule line 37 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:37
A question carries at most one provisional line. A worked proposal for settling it is a decision Spec whose Decision section holds its decision, context, rationales, alternatives and consequences, stated at the rung its record earns. Each shaped Spec names it through decidedBy, so a decision below defined holds that Spec below ready under the typed-dependency floor.
rule line 38 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:38
A re-entry trigger is one line naming what brings a deferred Spec back, such as a named reader the shipped views do not serve. It sits on the blocking question that holds the deferral, and the open-question register reports questions that carry one apart from design holds, so no reader tells the two apart by their wording.
rule line 39 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:39
An open question carries no status, date, blocked work unit or record of who checked it. A settled question leaves the Spec, a ruling that passes the ADR three-part test lands as a decision Spec the shaped Specs name through decidedBy, and the rest of the history stays in git and in the adopter's own records.
rule line 40 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:40
Whether a question holds the readiness floor stays its [blocking] flag alone; none of the four fields moves a floor.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.adopt-the-nouns

    The Protocol adopts established delivery nouns and rejects process state-machine and lifecycle gating.

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

Delivery sessions do the requested work on current graph evidence

spec:consumers.delivery-session-on-rampUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/delivery-session-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A handoff names the Specs that carry the work, so the next session re-measures them from the graph instead of inheriting register state or a verification verdict from the handoff.

Intent
outcome
Let an agent do the requested delivery work (capture, design, implement, fix, refactor, test, review, close, hand off) on current graph evidence, without inventing workflow state or gates.
Behavior
rule.advisoryShapes line 37 · specs/consumers/delivery-session-on-ramp.sdp.md:37
Work shapes are advisory entries over one current graph, never phases or a required sequence, and a session may enter or revisit any shape; no shape or preflight authorizes, blocks, scopes or advances delivery work.

no example exercises it

rule.taskSelectsShape line 38 · specs/consumers/delivery-session-on-ramp.sdp.md:38
The requested task selects the work shape. The roadmap's need and a Spec's promotion preflight are evidence about unfinished realization, never permission: a fix, a refactor, an added test or a change to a built Spec is ordinary work. The skill names the recipes a shape starts from and points into the catalog's index for the rest.

no example exercises it

rule.designLoop line 39 · specs/consumers/delivery-session-on-ramp.sdp.md:39
The skill teaches an advisory Pack design loop: read the design diff from the last pass, compose a context bundle within a stated budget, narrow by perspective when needed, and return a change proposal for a base check before an agent applies it.

no example exercises it

rule.buildFromSpec line 40 · specs/consumers/delivery-session-on-ramp.sdp.md:40
The skill teaches building a Spec from its graph context: read the law it rests on, what it guarantees and who verifies it, the open questions on it and on each Spec it rests on, its pinned declarations, its keyed rules no enabled example exercises, and the Specs that refine it, which its brief leaves out, so work on the rest of a feature first settles which Specs it builds; write the verifying tests before the code; hold the code to the pinned declarations and rules, leaving private names, decomposition and the algorithm to the build. The build proceeds on a non-blocking question's provisional reading and leaves the question open; a blocking question, or a non-blocking one with no provisional reading, goes to its decider, or to whoever gave the work when it names none, and the code that answers it waits while work that does not depend on it goes on; a choice the Spec leaves open without a question returns to the Spec as a question or a change proposal, never settled in code. Close reads the Spec's delivery facts and the drift alarm, which lists a Spec built below ready until its owner states the rung, so the handoff names each listed Spec and states no rung for the owner. Building below ready stays ordinary work.

Design view

Requirement drawing

  • Declared verifying examples: no declared verifying example.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

17. Composed intent hands off on one proposal shape

spec:consumers.intent-composition

Composed intent hands off on one proposal shape

spec:consumers.intent-compositionUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:agent-on-ramps-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/intent-composition.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding none, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The edit model, spec:consumers.edit-model, owns the intent, agent and git law. This Spec owns how a composing surface hands its intent off.

Intent
actor
A person or an agent reading a view who wants a design change made.
problem
Each composing surface could invent its own hand-off, so a reviewer, an agent and a check would read one change in as many shapes as there are surfaces.
outcome
Give every surface that composes scoped intent one hand-off shape, applied as an ordinary edit.
Behavior
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.sdp.md:19
Every surface that composes scoped intent, including the Studio's composing panel, hands off on the one change-proposal contract, spec:consumers.intent-composition.proposal.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.sdp.md:20
A composing surface writes no source.
rule.changedScope line 21 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.sdp.md:21
A composed proposal is applied after its proposal check: the applying caller sends a change whose scope changed since the base to a person instead of applying it and applies every other change as an ordinary edit, so one changed scope never holds back the whole proposal; the edit lands only from a worktree whose validation report, read through sdp q's report or sdp validate, holds no error, and the conformance and honesty checks stay the only gate.

no example exercises it

2 unkeyed rules.

18. The Studio skill teaches agents to publish, share and read the Spec Studio

spec:consumers.studio-on-ramp

The Studio skill teaches agents to publish, share and read the Spec Studio

spec:consumers.studio-on-rampUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

specs/consumers/studio-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The Studio's work reaches an agent in three forms: a person or an agent holding only a link, a coding agent that publishes pages or receives intent a person composed in them, and a developer who sets up previews in CI. Each needs steps that most graph questions never use, so the Studio has its own skill and the reading skill points to it.

Intent
outcome
Give an agent a shipped on-ramp that publishes and shares the Spec Studio, reads it by task from a repository or a link, and turns intent composed in it into checked carrier edits.
Behavior

specs/consumers/vault-on-ramp.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A person keeps the vault open beside an agent's design pass and writes notes of their own in it. The agent has to place and refresh the vault without touching those notes, recover a refused run without losing them, and turn them into carrier edits. None of that belongs in the on-ramp for graph questions, so the vault has its own skill and the reading skill points to it.

Intent
outcome
Give an agent a shipped on-ramp that places, synchronizes and recovers the Obsidian vault without losing a person's notes, and turns the intent a person writes there into checked carrier edits.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.vault-owned-folder

    The vault's generator owns one folder of the vault, sdp/, and keeps there a file list naming every file it wrote with a hash of its content. A .DS_Store file under sdp/ is ignored. A listed .base file a person changed is kept, even when it leaves the generated set, with its recorded content unchanged in the list; the run warns with its path and the words delete it to regenerate and goes on. For every other file, a run refuses, writing and removing nothing, while that folder holds a file the list does not name or one whose content the list does not record. Otherwise it synchronizes the folder: it writes the files whose content changed, leaves the others untouched, and removes the files it wrote that the graph no longer holds. The vault is not one of the projection roots the shared build rewrites: no build removes it, a vault directory where the build writes or removes is refused, and only the vault's synchronization writes it, whether sdp vault or the verb that writes every projection root runs it.

20. Every view run rewrites the view wholesale

spec:consumers.wholesale-view-rewrite

Every view run rewrites the view wholesale
