Design: no design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Guarantee that whatever a reader finds in the view directory was produced by the last run over the current source.
Rule
rule line 18 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:18
A view run rewrites the view wholesale: no page written by an earlier run survives a later one, so a Spec that left the corpus leaves no page behind.
rule line 19 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:19
Pages are written to a temporary sibling of the view directory, the previous directory is removed, and the temporary is renamed into place — one rename, so no half-written view is ever readable and no temporary survives a completed run.
rule line 20 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:20
A run that cannot produce a current view removes the stale one when its output parent remains safe instead of leaving it readable as current: an absent view is honest, a stale view is not.
rule.buildInvalidates line 21 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:21
Before extraction, the shared build removes generated/design-review/, generated/census/, generated/mermaid/ and generated/gherkin/, each with its temporary sibling, so a run that fails before rendering leaves no view behind; a removal failure refuses the build before extraction. Every command that enters this build, including validate and its watch runs and every publisher, has this invalidation effect, so a sibling root the command does not publish stays absent until a later publication. The Studio's root is removed beside these four, as spec:consumers.spec-studio.publisher states.

no example exercises it

rule line 22 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:22
Under --check-clean the view is rendered twice from the same graph and the run refuses when the two renders diverge, removing the view it could not certify.
rule line 23 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:23
Validation findings never withhold the view; publication refusals remain separate. A run whose checks report findings still writes the current view and returns the checks' own exit code, because the view is where those findings are read in context.
rule.portablePublication line 25 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:25
A case-insensitive page-path collision refuses the publisher's whole page set, names both ids and paths, removes its stale live and temporary roots when their parents are safe, and exits 1 regardless of validation's exit code. Renderers retain their page names and bytes.

no example exercises it

rule.safeCleanup line 26 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:26
Publication and failure cleanup recheck the physical output parent before each mutation; an escaping, unresolvable or linked generated/ parent is refused without cleanup through it.

no example exercises it

rule.osMetadata line 27 · specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.sdp.md:27
A file an operating system or a tool writes for its own use anywhere under a projection root, one whose whole name matches the junk package's list, such as Finder's .DS_Store or Windows's Thumbs.db, is never a page: --check-clean leaves it out when it reads the published root, so a root a file browser has shown still certifies, while any other file the run did not write, a file inside a directory of such a name included, still fails the check. Removing a root retries a bounded number of times when a folder gains such a file during the removal.

specs/consumers/wholesale-view-rewrite.validate-page-roots.sdp.md

1 open question and 1 blocking question; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

sdp validate enters the shared build, so it removes the five generated page roots before extraction and writes none of them back. It names none of the roots it removed, so a session that runs it to read findings loses the pages it was reading without being told.

Intent
outcome
Let a person or a CI job that runs sdp validate keep the pages it was reading, or learn from the run which page roots it removed.

specs/model/anchors.markdown-deliverable.sdp.md

1 open question and 1 blocking question; implementation binding none, verifier binding none, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The extractor reads anchors only from .ts and .tsx files, so a Markdown deliverable such as a shipped skill or a handbook binds through the document-realization binding: the suite that asserts the document carries the code anchor. The graph never names the Markdown file itself, so a change to it impacts no Spec and reports as coverage-unknown.

Intent
outcome
Let a Markdown deliverable, such as a shipped skill or a handbook, carry its own anchor, so the graph names the file and changed-file impact reaches the Specs it realizes.
